content:
It is now the last two months of the Mathlib Initiative year 1 roadmap https://mathlib-initiative.org/roadmap/ . It is not clear to me whether it is still being followed or how much progress were made. I understand that a lot of things have changed over the past year, and a roadmap isn't set in stone; still, to an outsider it looks like deviation from some of objectives and milestones listed there. For example, I couldn't find quarterly reviews, and specifically for reports on review response time. Going with anecdotal data, it feels worse than last year.

What is Mathlib Initiative's plan on these objectives?

Thanks for asking! You're right that public quarterly reports on e.g. the review performance was in the roadmap; indeed, no such reports exist yet. I have passed this on to the right people at the MI, they are aware of this and are working on a report that's suitable for public sharing. (There are internal reports, but these contain some yet-confidential information, so cannot be shared unedited.)
There is also work underway on a roadmap for the second year, which will be published once it is complete.

I agree there is a review crisis, with latencies being higher than e.g. in January. (I'm not sure it's worse than last year; the situation felt markedly better e.g. September through January.) It's a complicated topic with many factors. I (personally) also wish I had easy answers! Some plans include better tooling to help reviewers, growing the pool of reviewers (the mathlib review bootcamp helped, hopefully there will be another edition next year) and surely many things I don't remember right now.
